Section: section_1 — Prerequisite & Intuition: The 'Language' of Coordinates

Lecture lines:
A basis acts as your coordinate system's grid. [Asset: grid_01]
Standard vectors i and j define your directions. [Asset: vectors_01]
Point (3, 2) is a simple set of instructions. [Asset: point_01]

Planned animations:
Display a coordinate grid centered at (0,0) in #FFFFFF.
Place two basis vectors, e1 (1,0) and e2 (0,1) in #FF0000.
Show a point P(3,2) as a Dot in #00FF00.
Draw dashed lines from P to axes in #FFFF00.
Fade out the dashed lines and reset the grid.

Section: section_2 — The Problem: Changing Perspectives

Lecture lines:
Now introduce a new, tilted basis system. [Asset: tilt_01]
The point remains stationary in space. [Asset: static_point_01]
Coordinates change to describe the same location. [Asset: new_coords_01]

Planned animations:
Display two different basis sets, B1 and B2, in #FFFFFF.
Draw vector v represented in B1 basis in #00FFFF.
Show v transforming/rotating into B2 basis in #FF00FF.

Section: section_3 — The Mechanism: The Transition Matrix (P)

Lecture lines:
Transition matrix P translates between different bases. [Asset: matrix_p_01]
Columns of P are new basis vectors. [Asset: columns_01]
Apply [v]old = P * [v]new for conversion. [Asset: equation_01]
Visualize the mapping process between two grids. [Asset: mapping_01]
Example: P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]] maps coordinates. [Asset: example_01]

Planned animations:
Show matrix P in #FFFFFF.
Animate columns of P as basis vectors of B2 in #00FF00.
Multiply P by coordinates of v in B2 to get B1.

Section: section_4 — Application: Why Do We Care?

Lecture lines:
Choose bases to simplify complex mathematical calculations. [Asset: simplify_01]
Diagonalization makes shapes appear as simple rectangles. [Asset: rectangle_01]
Robots use local bases for easier control. [Asset: robot_01]

Planned animations:
Display a complex system, e.g., a rotating object.
Show how changing basis simplifies the representation.
Highlight the simplified matrix in #00FFFF.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Reflection

Lecture lines:
Basis is just a coordinate system choice. [Asset: recap_01]
Transition matrices act as system translators. [Asset: translator_01]
Perspective changes, but the space remains invariant. [Asset: invariant_01]

Planned animations:
Flash the title: Changing Perspectives.
Highlight the Transition Matrix P in #FF0000.
Show coordinate mapping concept again in #FFFFFF.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
